name: Kids Curiosity
origin: Existing idea P140; explicitly selected by the user, independently of ranking
user: A parent pays for a child aged roughly 6–10; they explore together initially.
first_result: The child predicts an answer to a why-question, manipulates a simple demonstration, and explains the result.
loop: Choose a reviewed why-question
Predict and explore one interactive explanation
Check the prediction and explain what changed
Return to a saved follow-up question or next short investigation
return_trigger: New child questions and a family discovery ritual; sustained return remains a hypothesis.
paid_value: An expanding, reviewed library of connected investigations and remembered interests, with useful follow-up questions.

pricing.basis: Hypothesis: USD6/month; no observed willingness to pay.
pricing.free: Three complete investigations without an account.
pricing.paid: Full reviewed library, saved paths and new investigation releases.

dependencies: Illustration/audio rights and factual source review
Parent-controlled account and age-appropriate data handling
compute: Curated explanations and local interactive diagrams; no live generative chat. Pilot library capped at 20 investigations and no per-session model calls.
content_burden: High: explanations, misconceptions, narration and usable interactions require review. Start one coherent question cluster; do not promise encyclopedic coverage.
first_scope: Question shelf covering a single everyday-science cluster
Saved follow-ups and a parent recap
acquisition: Test a publicly shareable one-question demonstration with parent audiences; access and acquisition cost are unverified.

competitors.name: Mystery Science
competitors.facts: Elementary science curriculum combines question-led lessons, investigations and activities; the site offers a free trial.
competitors.price: Paid price not verified.

competitors.name: Science for Kids by Tappity
competitors.facts: Developer listing describes interactive, narrated science lessons, daily challenges, offline use and parent discussion prompts.
competitors.price: US App Store lists multiple subscription SKUs; a single currently offered checkout price was not verified.

difference: Test a tightly connected predict–explore–explain path around a child's question, with a visible end. Tappity already serves curiosity; this is a UX hypothesis, not an empty market.
risk: Incumbents already supply interactive answers and recurring lessons. Editorial production can dominate software costs, while a generic chatbot is a free substitute.
experiment: Give parents one complete unaided investigation; observe whether the child explains it and chooses another later without researcher prompting; then offer a clearly priced reviewed collection.
stop_rule: Pause expansion if children only consume narration, parents must teach the interface, or returning families decline paid access in favor of existing resources.
overlap: Other STEM entries teach specific subject skills; this serves family why-questions. Do not split topic packs into separate products. Excludes Pose Coach and Hijinx.
rationale: Immediate demonstration and repeat curiosity fit the brief; paid retention and differentiation are unproven. User selection does not raise the score.
confidence: low; competitor evidence only, user selection is not demand validation

name: Formula Drill Gym
origin: Existing idea P037, narrowed to independent browser practice
user: An individual spreadsheet user pays to become reliable with formulas without connecting a workplace workbook.
first_result: Solve a small spreadsheet task and see why a formula succeeds or fails on unseen rows.
loop: Choose a concrete spreadsheet outcome
Write a formula in a small browser grid
Inspect result differences and targeted hints
Revisit a weak skill through a new dataset
return_trigger: Recurring spreadsheet use and spaced practice; upskilling may instead be a finite course purchase.
paid_value: Diagnostic exercises, varied test data, error explanations and a maintained practice path beyond reference documentation.

pricing.basis: Hypothesis: USD6/month; test against a one-time course because completion churn is plausible.
pricing.free: A complete beginner diagnostic and its correction exercises.
pricing.paid: Full practice paths, error history and fresh mixed-skill challenges.

dependencies: Licensed or compatible spreadsheet formula engine
Spreadsheet educator review and cross-engine semantics checks
compute: Local formula evaluation on synthetic sheets capped at 200 cells per exercise; no uploaded workbooks or AI calls.
content_burden: Moderate: author realistic datasets, accepted equivalent answers, edge cases and hints. Choose one formula dialect first.
first_scope: Browser grid with a small supported formula set
acquisition: Publish an ungated formula challenge with its error explanation; measure qualified practice starts from spreadsheet tutorial audiences. No audience access established.

competitors.name: Excel Exercises
competitors.facts: Paid practice includes interactive tutorials, exercises, assessments and downloadable data.
competitors.price: Page displays $19.99/month, $59.99 billed yearly, and $199 lifetime; dollar currency code is not shown.

competitors.name: Excel Practice Online
competitors.facts: Provides free browser-based Excel practice across beginner and advanced topics.
competitors.price: Free practice is advertised; no paid price verified.

difference: Test feedback showing the smallest failing data example and resurfacing that error later. Interactive spreadsheet practice is already available commercially and free.
risk: A one-time learning burst may not support MRR; mature free exercises and reference assistants already answer common formula questions.
experiment: Offer a complete formula diagnostic without setup; watch a later unprompted mixed exercise; compare actual purchase of monthly practice with a clearly bounded course offer.
stop_rule: Reject subscription if learners finish their immediate gap and do not return, or if they prefer free practice after trying the distinctive feedback.
overlap: E024 teaches database querying; E016 teaches interpretation. No workplace import, team dashboard or custom workbook service.
rationale: Excellent immediate browser value and bounded compute; recurrence and novelty are materially weaker than implementation feasibility.

name: Hifz Revision Companion
origin: Existing idea P057; remove teacher-management workflow from initial scope
user: An independent Quran memorizer pays for sustainable revision of passages already learned.
first_result: Mark familiar passages and complete a short recall session that creates tomorrow's revision queue.
loop: Choose memorized portions and available revision time
Recall from concealed text and mark hesitation
Compare against the licensed text and record self-assessed difficulty
Return when specific passages are due
return_trigger: Maintaining memorized material requires continuing revision; adoption of this particular scheduler is unverified.
paid_value: A flexible revision schedule, mistake-location history and recovery after missed days without manually rebuilding a plan.

pricing.basis: Hypothesis: USD4/month; no observed willingness to pay.
pricing.free: One memorized section with a working revision loop.
pricing.paid: Larger revision library, flexible scheduling and history across devices.

dependencies: Verified Quran text and permitted recitation assets if included
Hifz practitioner review of scheduling and presentation
Access to independent memorizers for validation is not established
compute: Local scheduling and text conceal/reveal; no automated recitation recognition in the pilot. Cap optional downloaded audio to selected sections.
content_burden: Moderate specialist burden: accurate text mapping, respectful presentation, revision methods and accessibility; no generated religious interpretation.
first_scope: Adaptive self-rated review queue with missed-day recovery
acquisition: Demonstrate recovery from an overloaded revision queue to independent memorizer communities; distribution permission and access are unverified.

competitors.name: Tarteel Premium
competitors.facts: Premium includes memorization mistake detection, planning, historical mistakes and peeking; monthly and yearly renewals are described.
competitors.price: Premium amount not verified.

competitors.name: Quranly
competitors.facts: Provides reading goals, progress tracking, daily streaks and optional friend/family participation.
competitors.price: Site offers free starting access; paid plan price not verified.

difference: Test a quiet self-assessed revision queue designed around missed-day recovery. Tarteel already combines planning and mistake history; superiority is unproven.
risk: Tarteel offers more capable recitation feedback, and a notebook or free scheduler may be sufficient. Religious expertise and trusted distribution cannot be replaced by code.
experiment: Let existing memorizers configure real known passages unaided, use the due queue through a missed day, then choose whether to buy ongoing scheduling at the stated price.
stop_rule: Stop if learners cannot trust self-assessment, require speech correction to find value, or return to their existing revision routine despite successful onboarding.
overlap: E022 serves arbitrary study notes; this handles passage continuity and memorization maintenance. Not a mosque/teacher administration product.
rationale: Natural continuing revision is stronger than a finite course; competition, trust and unverified buyer access restrain the opportunity.

name: Phonics-to-Reading Path
user: A parent of an early reader pays for structured decoding practice at home.
first_result: A child blends a taught sound pattern and independently decodes a short matching sentence.
loop: Check a small set of known sounds
Blend and read decodable words
Hear the model and retry a missed pattern
Unlock a short text using retained patterns
return_trigger: Regular reading development during a finite learning stage; long-term subscription retention is not assumed.
paid_value: A coherent, reviewed decoding sequence and texts that match the child's taught patterns.

pricing.basis: Hypothesis: USD25 per complete beginner course; zero subscription MRR.
pricing.free: One sound-pattern lesson and matching story.
pricing.paid: A finite sequenced decoding course with progress storage.

compute: Pre-recorded audio and local interaction; no voice diagnosis. Cap first course at one progression of sound patterns.
content_burden: High: phonics sequence, decodability, accents and accessibility require careful expert review.
acquisition: Offer a complete parent-child decoding sample to early-reading audiences; acquisition and trust are unverified.

competitors.name: Reading Eggs
competitors.facts: Offers interactive reading lessons, phonics activities, games and a digital book library for home learning.
competitors.price: Free trial advertised; paid price not verified.

difference: Test a small, transparent course where each story shows the sound patterns it practices. No claim that established curricula lack this.
risk: A well-known curriculum with a broad library is easier for parents to trust; pedagogy and content production are harder than the app.
experiment: Observe a parent starting the sample without training, the child using a new sentence later, and an actual decision to buy the bounded course.
stop_rule: Defer if expert review cannot be secured, children guess from pictures instead of decoding, or parents choose an existing curriculum after the sample.
overlap: E023 targets comprehension conversations with fluent-enough readers; E004 teaches decoding. Not a generalized child tutor.
rationale: Clear observable outcome but high specialist burden and crowded paid alternatives; honest finite-course pricing.

name: Fraction Sense Lab
user: A parent or self-directed learner pays to understand fraction magnitude and operations visually.
first_result: Construct two equivalent fractions and explain why their sizes match.
loop: Make a prediction about a fraction relationship
Manipulate area and number-line models
Compare the visual result with the numerical answer
Revisit a misconception in a different representation
return_trigger: A finite sequence of misconceptions plus review before later mathematics; not an endless-content assumption.
paid_value: A complete conceptual progression linking fractions to magnitude, equivalence and operations.

pricing.basis: Hypothesis: USD15 for the complete fraction course; zero subscription MRR.
pricing.paid: Full fraction progression and mixed review.

compute: Local geometry and exact rational arithmetic; bounded authored problems, no generative grading.
content_burden: Moderate: carefully chosen misconception examples, transfer questions and explanatory visuals.
acquisition: Share a visual fraction misconception challenge with parents searching for a concrete explanation; channel access unverified.

competitors.name: Math Makers
competitors.facts: Uses physics-based puzzles to teach mathematics including fractions and offers family membership.
competitors.price: Membership amount not verified.

difference: Test explicit transfer between a manipulated model and a symbolic explanation; an unvalidated instructional emphasis, not a claim of unique fraction games.
risk: A narrow topic finishes quickly and competes with free lessons plus polished games; playful success may not transfer to actual reasoning.
experiment: Give the first lesson unaided, check a different representation in a later session, then offer the completed course for purchase.
stop_rule: Stop if learners solve the game but cannot transfer the concept, or if interested parents will only use free samples.
overlap: A coherent conceptual course rather than another generic drill bank; topic packs are not separate candidate products.
rationale: Demonstrable and inexpensive to run; limited duration and curriculum quality constrain revenue and feasibility.

name: Programming Puzzle Workshop
user: A beginner learner or parent pays for a first coding course that produces working behaviors in a browser.
first_result: Write a short program that changes a visible simulation and repair one failing case.
loop: Choose a behavior to create
Edit a small program and run it
Inspect execution and a failing example
Apply the concept to a new behavior
return_trigger: A structured beginner course followed by optional new project packs; not indefinite drill retention.
paid_value: A reliable progression from sequences to functions, with visual execution and testable small creations.

pricing.basis: Hypothesis: USD25 per beginner course; zero subscription MRR.
pricing.paid: Full introductory course and project exports.

compute: Run a restricted language locally with execution-step and memory caps; no cloud execution or model hints.
content_burden: Moderate to high: projects, test cases, trace explanations and frustration management.
first_scope: Small local code editor and runner
Three connected projects using the same concepts
acquisition: Demonstrate a learner changing a simulation with five lines of code; test starts from beginner-coding audiences.

competitors.name: CodeCombat
competitors.facts: Premium adds characters, scripting/game-building features and AI hints; the page describes a daily hint allowance.
competitors.price: Paid price not verified.

difference: Test debugging through a visible failing execution trace, with tiny creations rather than a large game world. Similar teaching mechanics may already exist.
risk: Free coding education and polished game-based incumbents set a high bar; motivation can collapse as puzzles become syntax-heavy.
experiment: Observe a learner creating and debugging the free project unaided, returning for a second project, and purchasing the complete course.
stop_rule: Stop if meaningful completion repeatedly needs live tutoring or learners can follow instructions but cannot modify a new behavior.
overlap: E024 teaches relational data reasoning, not general programming. Excludes job interview preparation and creative game-making platforms.
rationale: Bounded computation and visible output fit self-serve adoption; content and differentiation remain substantial work.

name: Household Science Simulator
user: A parent or curious learner pays for guided virtual experiments about everyday physical phenomena.
first_result: Change one variable in a simulated experiment and identify its effect from observed measurements.
loop: Form a prediction from a specific question
Change a controlled variable
Read a measurement and revise the explanation
Try a transfer investigation using the same principle
return_trigger: A series of investigations during a science-learning phase; new packs need genuine new concepts.
paid_value: Coherent guided experiment packs with misconceptions, measurements and clear explanations.

pricing.basis: Hypothesis: USD18 per reviewed experiment pack; zero subscription MRR.
pricing.paid: A connected pack with replayable measurement tasks.

compute: Local simplified physics models with explicitly stated assumptions; fixed scenes and no generative video.
content_burden: High: simulations must be educationally honest and explanations must distinguish a model from reality.
first_scope: A small heat/light or force investigation set
acquisition: Publish one surprising predict-then-test interaction; assess whether families choose a connected paid pack.

competitors.name: PhET Interactive Simulations
competitors.facts: University of Colorado Boulder provides free research-based interactive science and mathematics simulations, usable online or by download.
competitors.price: Free simulations are explicitly described.

difference: Test a short guided home-learning sequence around a single principle. Free PhET activities already provide strong interactive alternatives.
risk: Free, research-based simulations may be better than a solo builder can produce; this can collapse into a topic pack of Kids Curiosity.
experiment: Test whether learners complete a measurement investigation unaided and later use the principle in a different case before buying the full pack.
stop_rule: Consolidate into E001 if users perceive only another curiosity topic; stop if models need continual explanation by an adult.
overlap: Explicit consolidation candidate with E001. Keep separate only if measured experimentation, not question discovery, drives purchase.
rationale: Attractive demonstration but weak subscription logic, free alternatives and substantial overlap.

name: Pronunciation Practice Lab
user: An adult language learner pays to distinguish and produce a small set of difficult speech sounds.
first_result: Hear a minimal-pair contrast, record both sounds, and identify the difference against a reviewed model.
loop: Choose a sound contrast from a short diagnostic
Listen, discriminate and record fixed phrases
Compare playback with annotated model audio
Revisit weak contrasts through new fixed phrases
return_trigger: Repeated practice while improving intelligibility; long-term usage beyond a pronunciation course is uncertain.
paid_value: Expert-selected contrasts, high-quality model audio and a structured listening-to-production progression.

pricing.basis: Hypothesis: USD20 per language-specific pronunciation course; zero subscription MRR.
pricing.free: One complete contrast with listening and recording.
pricing.paid: A reviewed course with a personal replay history.

compute: Record and replay locally; fixed audio assets. No claimed accent scoring or automatic correctness in the pilot; recordings remain bounded to selected exercises.
content_burden: High: language-specific contrasts, accents, models and clear mouth-position instruction require expertise.
first_scope: Scheduled review of self-rated weak contrasts
acquisition: Demonstrate an easy-to-hear contrast to language-learning audiences; test completion without teacher assistance.

competitors.name: ELSA Speak
competitors.facts: Offers personalized English practice, feedback, learning paths, roleplay and progress tracking.
competitors.price: Free starting access is advertised; paid price not verified.

difference: Test a tightly bounded listening-and-production course with transparent audio comparison. ELSA already offers much richer feedback.
risk: Without trustworthy automatic feedback, users may prefer free audio or a teacher; adding speech scoring creates cost and accuracy risk.
experiment: Have learners finish a contrast exercise unaided, repeat it independently later, and purchase a course only if the comparison helps them self-correct.
stop_rule: Stop if learners cannot judge their own improvement or demand automated scoring before they find the product useful.
overlap: Root's speaking rehearsal covers presentations/conversations. This teaches foreign-language phonemes, not public speaking or Pose Coach.
rationale: Clear skill outcome but expert content and feedback quality are central; a cheap audio wrapper is insufficient.

name: Graded Reading Language Club
user: An intermediate language learner pays to finish enjoyable reading at an appropriate difficulty.
first_result: Finish a short graded chapter, understand its main event and retain several useful phrases.
loop: Choose a story at a tested reading level
Read with optional reviewed audio and selective glosses
Check understanding and retrieve useful phrases
Return for the next chapter and spaced phrase review
return_trigger: Continuing stories and repeated exposure to a language; ongoing demand for this catalogue is unverified.
paid_value: A consistent stream of enjoyable, level-controlled stories with audio and purposeful phrase review.

pricing.basis: Hypothesis: USD7/month; no observed willingness to pay.
pricing.free: One complete short story with audio and review.
pricing.paid: Full serial catalogue, new chapters and cross-story review.

dependencies: Original or licensed fiction and narration
compute: Local reader and review scheduling with cached audio; no live translation or generated stories. Bound the pilot to one completed serial.
content_burden: High ongoing editorial and narration work; quality, natural language and level consistency are the product.
acquisition: Release one satisfying story with a shareable first chapter through language-learning audiences; audience access is unverified.

competitors.name: LingQ
competitors.facts: Combines reading/listening, imported or library content, vocabulary progress and AI-supported language tools.
competitors.price: Free signup is offered; paid price not verified.

difference: Test a deliberately small, editor-authored serial with a clear next episode and limited glossing. Existing readers already offer extensive libraries.
risk: Free native content and established readers dwarf a small catalogue; constant publishing may cost more than the app can support.
experiment: Let learners complete a free story unaided, return for a later chapter, and buy access to the finished serial at the stated subscription price.
stop_rule: Switch to finite story packs or stop if readers binge once, do not return for vocabulary, or mainly want arbitrary content imports.
overlap: E023 is parent-child first-language comprehension; this serves adult second-language reading. No separate product per language.
rationale: A plausible serial habit, but editorial throughput and a crowded category limit solo-builder appeal.

name: Sign-Language Practice Path
user: A hearing beginner pays to learn introductory signs for everyday communication with a specific signing community.
first_result: Recognize a short signed exchange and reproduce a small set of signs against a video model.
loop: Start a situation-led lesson in one sign language
Watch, recognize and reproduce signs
Compare recording with signer-led guidance
Review and combine signs in a later exchange
return_trigger: Practice during a finite beginner course and real communication opportunities; learning one course need not recur indefinitely.
paid_value: A coherent Deaf-led introduction with authentic examples, slow playback and structured review.

pricing.basis: Hypothesis: USD30 for a reviewed beginner course; zero subscription MRR.
pricing.paid: A bounded course with signed dialogues and review.

dependencies: Paid Deaf native-signer authorship and cultural review
compute: Pre-recorded video and local optional recording; no gesture-recognition promise. Cap storage to recent practice clips.
content_burden: Very high specialist video burden; sign languages differ and cannot be treated as simple word substitutions.
first_scope: One language and a small real-life situation sequence
acquisition: A signer-led sample lesson can demonstrate value; access to trusted educators and communities is not established.

competitors.name: Lingvano
competitors.facts: ASL lessons are taught by native Deaf signers and include dialogues, flashcards, a learning path and fingerspelling feedback.
competitors.price: Trial advertised; paid price not verified.

difference: Test a small situational course chosen with native signers; no claim that signer-led learning or camera feedback is new.
risk: A mature Deaf-led incumbent already has curriculum and recognition technology; without credible authors this should not be built.
experiment: Validate the lesson with native signers first, then observe beginner comprehension, later independent review and an actual course purchase.
stop_rule: Defer without an accountable content partner, or if learners need live correction to benefit from the self-serve lessons.
overlap: Distinct from spoken-language pronunciation; a complete communication course, not a theme variant of a flashcard app.
rationale: Useful independent outcome, but video authorship, cultural credibility and competition overwhelm software simplicity.

name: Braille Literacy Trainer
user: A sighted parent, helper or educator pays to learn visual braille transcription and recognition.
first_result: Read and type a short sequence of braille cells with accurate immediate correction.
loop: Learn a small cell pattern set
Read or chord a short phrase
Inspect cell-level corrections
Review uncertain patterns in later phrases
return_trigger: A finite literacy course plus occasional refresh; visual training does not establish tactile reading competence.
paid_value: A convenient, accessible course with practice passages and error-focused review.

pricing.basis: Hypothesis: USD12 for a complete introductory visual course; zero subscription MRR.
pricing.paid: Finite literacy progression and review history.

compute: Local symbol mapping and grading with small text passages; no hardware or AI required.
content_burden: High correctness burden despite small software scope: contractions, ambiguity, notation and accessibility matter.
acquisition: Demonstrate a complete keyboard lesson to family-support audiences; specialist-community access is unverified.

competitors.name: UEB Online
competitors.facts: NextSense offers braille literacy and mathematics training with accessibility modes and saved progress; a computer is required.
competitors.price: Courses are free; an optional completion certificate is AU$50.

difference: Test a more convenient practice experience for sighted helpers. Do not imply it replaces tactile instruction or that established training is unavailable.
risk: A credible free specialist provider already offers structured courses. A small convenience improvement may have no meaningful paid market.
experiment: Have target helpers complete a lesson unaided, return for a later phrase, and choose between the proposed paid course and UEB Online.
stop_rule: Stop if free UEB Online meets the same need or expert review finds the interface teaches misleading reading habits.
overlap: Different sensory literacy outcome from phonics; no hardware sales or assistive-device claims.
rationale: Bounded mechanics but finite demand, free specialist competition and a narrow unverified buyer group.

name: Logic and Proof Lab
user: A mathematically curious student pays to learn how to construct and challenge valid proofs.
first_result: Build a valid short argument and see a counterexample to an invalid inference.
loop: Inspect a proposition and available assumptions
Assemble justified proof steps
See which inference fails or why the proof closes
Tackle a later theorem reusing learned rules
return_trigger: Progression through a finite reasoning course with optional harder chapters.
paid_value: A carefully sequenced bridge from intuitive arguments to explicit proof rules.

pricing.basis: Hypothesis: USD20 for a foundational proof course; zero subscription MRR.
pricing.paid: A reviewed proof progression with saved attempts.

dependencies: A sound limited proof checker or licensed/open-source engine review
compute: Local checking in a bounded propositional or elementary-number domain; cap proof size and avoid arbitrary theorem search.
content_burden: High: proofs, hints, counterexamples and progression need careful correctness review.
first_scope: A connected sequence of elementary propositions
acquisition: Publish one surprising invalid-argument puzzle and a complete correction path; test interest from self-directed mathematics learners.

competitors.name: Natural Number Game
competitors.facts: The official repository implements the Natural Number Game in Lean 4 using a game engine for interactive proof learning.
competitors.price: Source is publicly available; a paid access price is not listed on this repository.

difference: Test an introductory visual bridge before formal syntax. Interactive proof-learning games already exist; the bridge must prove its instructional value.
risk: Free formal-proof games and textbooks serve motivated learners; easy puzzles may fail to teach genuine proof construction.
experiment: Observe an unaided proof, a later unfamiliar theorem using the same rule, and purchase of the complete course.
stop_rule: Stop if learners only rearrange hints or cannot explain validity outside the interface, or prefer the free formal game.
overlap: Not a recreational puzzle collection: success is transferable proof construction. E016 evaluates empirical data rather than deductive validity.
rationale: Distinct educational outcome but niche reach and demanding content validation.

name: Molecule Builder
user: A chemistry learner pays to understand bonding and spatial molecular structure through construction.
first_result: Build a target molecule that satisfies a limited bonding rule set and inspect its spatial form.
loop: Read a structural target or constraint
Place atoms and bonds
Inspect valence feedback and a reviewed 3D model
Solve a later construction with a new constraint
return_trigger: A bounded chemistry-learning unit and revision before assessments.
paid_value: Guided construction problems that connect notation, bonding constraints and spatial understanding.

pricing.basis: Hypothesis: USD18 for an introductory structure course; zero subscription MRR.
pricing.paid: Reviewed structure challenges and concept review.

dependencies: Permitted molecule geometry data and rendering library
compute: Local graph checks and display of reviewed geometries; no quantum chemistry or arbitrary structure prediction. Limit atom types and molecule size.
content_burden: High scientific correctness burden; simplified bonding rules must be labeled and carefully bounded.
acquisition: Demonstrate how a correct flat formula can conceal a spatial misconception to chemistry-learning audiences.

competitors.name: MolView
competitors.facts: Provides a molecular structure editor, interactive 3D visualization and database lookup for chemical structures.
competitors.price: A premium version is referenced; exact pricing not verified.

difference: Test a guided construction-and-explanation course around a bounded set of misconceptions, rather than general molecule viewing.
risk: Free or established visualization tools plus lessons may suffice; inaccurate simplifications would undermine the educational outcome.
experiment: Observe construction of a first molecule and a later transfer problem, then offer the completed course for actual purchase.
stop_rule: Stop if users need arbitrary research molecules rather than the bounded course, or expert review cannot validate the feedback.
overlap: Distinct from E007's controlled-variable experiments and E021's anatomy orientation; no research or clinical tool claims.
rationale: Strong visual activation but finite use and demanding specialist validation.

name: Geography Recall Expeditions
user: A curious learner or parent pays for durable geographic understanding beyond isolated capital trivia.
first_result: Reconstruct a small region on a map and explain one relationship between its terrain and settlements.
loop: Explore a region through map layers
Rebuild missing locations and relationships
Compare against the map and explain an error
Revisit weak spatial relationships in a new route
return_trigger: Sequential region study and spaced spatial recall; completion is finite.
paid_value: Coherent map-based learning journeys and a personal review path.

pricing.basis: Hypothesis: USD15 for a complete geography course pack; zero subscription MRR.
pricing.paid: Connected map reconstruction journeys and review.

dependencies: Policy for disputed boundaries and changing names
compute: Local vector maps and answer checks; no live map API required. Cap to selected regions and reviewed datasets.
content_burden: Moderate ongoing corrections plus authored explanations; avoid multiplying country quiz skins.
acquisition: Share a playable map-reconstruction challenge with a meaningful explanation; test discovery through geography-learning audiences.

competitors.name: Lizard Point Geography
competitors.facts: Offers geography quizzes covering places, flags and bodies of water, alongside free printable maps.
competitors.price: Free printable maps are advertised; paid quiz pricing not verified.

difference: Test spatial reconstruction linked to causal geography explanations. Map quizzes already exist in abundance.
risk: Users may want casual free trivia rather than a paid learning path; proposed depth adds editorial work without proven willingness to pay.
experiment: Observe an unaided map reconstruction, a later route-transfer exercise, and an actual course-pack purchase.
stop_rule: Stop if users only replay familiar trivia or cannot transfer location knowledge to a different map view.
overlap: Play E063 teaches navigation in the real night sky. E014 teaches terrestrial spatial geography; no travel itinerary product.
rationale: Easy to demonstrate and cheap to run; crowded free category and finite progression weaken monetization.

name: History Cause-and-Effect Atlas
user: A curious adult or older student pays to understand the chronology and competing explanations of historical change.
first_result: Build an evidence-linked timeline and distinguish a supported causal claim from mere sequence.
loop: Enter a bounded historical question
Arrange events and inspect primary-source excerpts
Compare alternative causal explanations
Return for a connected episode or source challenge
return_trigger: Curiosity about connected periods and completion of a finite episode collection.
paid_value: Well-edited historical investigations with source context and honest treatment of uncertainty.

pricing.basis: Hypothesis: USD18 per reviewed historical collection; zero subscription MRR.
pricing.paid: A connected collection of investigations and maps.

dependencies: Rights and translations for source excerpts
compute: Local timelines, maps and authored branching; no generated historical claims or live fact retrieval.
content_burden: Very high: source selection, context, translations and contested interpretations require accountable scholarship.
acquisition: Publish a short historical misconception investigation with visible sources; audience access is unverified.

competitors.name: HistoryMaps
competitors.facts: Presents a visual history-learning project and a subscription supporting access for learners and educators.
competitors.price: Subscription amount not verified.

difference: Test a source-comparison learning path centered on causal reasoning; visual history itself is already served.
risk: A solo engineer cannot cheaply sustain authoritative historical publishing; free articles, videos and existing visual platforms are strong substitutes.
experiment: Have readers finish one source investigation unaided, return for its connected episode, and purchase the complete collection.
stop_rule: Defer without qualified editorial review or if users value only passive summaries available free elsewhere.
overlap: E017 examines modern information credibility; E015 reconstructs historical explanations using contextualized sources.
rationale: A distinct educational product, but editorial cost and weak recurring payment logic outweigh software appeal.

name: Data Literacy Detective
user: A nontechnical adult or older student pays to understand charts and numerical claims encountered in everyday reading.
first_result: Identify a misleading chart choice, correct it and explain how the interpretation changes.
loop: Inspect a numerical claim and its dataset
Manipulate scales, groups or denominators
Compare interpretations and identify the unsupported claim
Apply the principle to a new case
return_trigger: A finite foundation course followed by occasional new cases; constant subscription use is unverified.
paid_value: A practical course in data interpretation through manipulable examples and transfer tasks.

pricing.basis: Hypothesis: USD20 for a foundational course; zero subscription MRR.
pricing.paid: A reviewed course spanning denominators, uncertainty, sampling and chart choices.

compute: Local deterministic chart rendering and known-case feedback; no data uploads or model grading.
content_burden: Moderate to high: examples must accurately teach uncertainty without oversimplifying statistics.
first_scope: Later transfer cases with new data
acquisition: Share an interactive chart that changes the apparent conclusion when corrected; test completion from numeracy audiences.

competitors.name: DataCamp Introduction to Data Literacy
competitors.facts: A nontechnical course covers data quality, sources, bias, chart choice and communicating data through interactive exercises.
competitors.price: Free course start advertised; full paid access price not verified.

difference: Test short adversarial chart investigations for everyday readers. Existing data-literacy courses already teach these concepts.
risk: Strong free explanations and bundled courses may remove the reason to pay separately; a few tricks do not establish data literacy.
experiment: Observe one unaided correction and a later unfamiliar chart interpretation, followed by purchase of the complete course.
stop_rule: Stop if learners memorize visual tricks but cannot reason about a different denominator or uncertainty example.
overlap: E002 teaches spreadsheet formulas and E024 SQL; E016 teaches interpretation without tool syntax. E017 covers broader source credibility.
rationale: Excellent independence and bounded compute; finite course demand and limited distinctiveness keep it reserve.

name: Media Literacy Detective
user: An adult or parent of a teenager pays for practical source-evaluation learning.
first_result: Trace a claim through a contained source packet and identify what the evidence does and does not support.
loop: Inspect a plausible claim
Compare provenance, context and corroborating sources
Receive an evidence-based explanation
Investigate a later case using the same verification method
return_trigger: A finite set of literacy skills and occasional refresher cases; news consumption alone does not prove product recurrence.
paid_value: Carefully constructed investigations that teach reusable verification habits.

pricing.basis: Hypothesis: USD12 for a complete investigation pack; zero subscription MRR.
pricing.paid: A reviewed pack spanning source provenance, context and image reuse.

dependencies: Rights to source material or clearly labeled fictional cases
compute: Curated static evidence packets with local branching; no live automated fact-checking or unbounded web retrieval.
content_burden: High editorial burden: plausible evidence, balanced framing and supported explanations. Fictional cases reduce live-claim maintenance.
acquisition: Share a playable verification case through media-literacy audiences; no partner or school adoption assumed.

competitors.name: Checkology
competitors.facts: News Literacy Project provides interactive news-literacy lessons, including misinformation and verification activities, aimed at grades 5–12.
competitors.price: Free account and lessons are advertised.

difference: Test independent adult/family investigations in a compact consumer flow. Interactive news-literacy education already exists free.
risk: A credible nonprofit supplies free lessons; buyers may see literacy education as a public service or school responsibility rather than a purchase.
experiment: Observe an unaided case, a later novel source check and actual purchase of a finite pack after showing the free alternative.
stop_rule: Stop if users only enjoy guessing fake headlines or cannot transfer verification behavior beyond the authored case.
overlap: E016 isolates statistical reasoning; E025 constructs arguments. This evaluates provenance and corroboration, not political persuasion.
rationale: Clear self-serve learning but weak paid value against free specialist alternatives.

name: Touch-Typing Adventure
user: A beginner or parent pays to develop accurate touch typing through a bounded learning journey.
first_result: Complete a short keyboard task without looking down and see which keys caused errors.
loop: Start a brief placement exercise
Type an authored passage at a comfortable pace
Inspect accuracy and weak-key patterns
Return for a targeted passage and new story segment
return_trigger: Practice until usable typing proficiency; mature users may have little reason to continue paying.
paid_value: A coherent beginner course, targeted weak-key practice and a satisfying finite story.

pricing.basis: Hypothesis: USD10 for the complete course; zero subscription MRR.
pricing.free: Placement and a full first story segment.
pricing.paid: Finite story course and personalized key review.

dependencies: Keyboard-layout data and accessible input handling
compute: Local key timing and deterministic exercise selection; no AI or cloud media required.
content_burden: Moderate: graded passages, pacing, keyboard layouts and story quality.
acquisition: Release a short playable typing story; test whether beginner families purchase after trying a free incumbent.

competitors.name: TypingClub
competitors.facts: Free individual learning includes lessons, videos, games, stories and optional progress profiles; a paid school edition also exists.
competitors.price: Individual use is advertised as free; school pricing not verified.

difference: A proposed compact course emphasizing comfortable accuracy; TypingClub already has stories, games and progression, so novelty is weak.
risk: Free incumbents already provide the proposed experience, and typing improvement eventually removes the need.
experiment: Observe an unaided story session and later independent practice, then test an actual course purchase beside the free alternative.
stop_rule: Stop if users choose TypingClub after comparison or the story does not improve continued practice beyond a plain free drill.
overlap: Not a general productivity tracker or a separate product per keyboard layout. Finite skill learning is the purchase.
rationale: Easy to activate and operate, but near-identical free alternatives make commercial differentiation very weak.

name: Circuit Learning Lab
user: An electronics beginner pays to understand and diagnose simple circuits without purchasing hardware.
first_result: Repair a simulated circuit and explain the voltage or current observation that located its fault.
loop: Inspect a small faulty circuit and a target behavior
Measure and change a component
See the predicted electrical result and an explanation
Diagnose a later fault using the same principle
return_trigger: A finite foundational electronics course and optional advanced diagnostic packs.
paid_value: A well-sequenced set of fault-finding missions with measurements and validated explanations.

pricing.basis: Hypothesis: USD20 for a beginner circuit course; zero subscription MRR.
pricing.paid: A coherent progression of simulated faults and circuit concepts.

dependencies: Permitted circuit-simulation engine and numerical validation
compute: Local small-circuit solver; bound component count and timestep. No external hardware and no arbitrary high-voltage construction instructions.
content_burden: High technical correctness burden: plausible faults, numerical behavior and conceptual explanations.
acquisition: Demonstrate an apparently broken circuit solved through one measurement; test learners in beginner-electronics audiences.

competitors.name: Falstad Circuit Simulator
competitors.facts: Provides an animated electronic-circuit simulator with current/voltage visualization, editable parameters and sample circuits.
competitors.price: Public simulator page is accessible; no paid price is listed.

difference: Test a diagnostic course with explicit learning goals around the simulator. General circuit simulation is already accessible.
risk: Free simulators and tutorial videos may be sufficient; a trustworthy solver and curriculum take substantial validation.
experiment: Observe a learner diagnose the first fault unaided, solve a different fault later, and buy the full course.
stop_rule: Stop if learners guess component changes without using evidence or require live instruction to interpret the measurements.
overlap: Distinct circuit diagnosis outcome from E007's everyday experiments; no engineering design service or hardware kit.
rationale: Strong demonstration and bounded scope, but finite paid use and specialist verification remain constraints.

name: Astronomy Mission Lab
user: A curious learner or parent pays to understand orbital motion, phases and eclipses through virtual missions.
first_result: Arrange a simplified Sun–Earth–Moon model to predict a phase and verify it from two viewpoints.
loop: Accept a model-based astronomy question
Manipulate time and relative positions
Compare a prediction with the modeled observation
Return for a connected mission using the same model
return_trigger: A finite astronomy concept progression, with optional later mission packs.
paid_value: Guided predictive missions that connect spatial models to familiar astronomical observations.

pricing.basis: Hypothesis: USD15 for the complete introductory mission pack; zero subscription MRR.
pricing.paid: A connected set of phase, eclipse and orbital-motion missions.

dependencies: Permitted astronomical data or explicitly simplified models
compute: Local simplified orbital geometry with fixed bodies and labeled scale assumptions; no ephemeris service required for the pilot.
content_burden: Moderate to high: camera framing, scale caveats and misconception checks must be scientifically sound.
acquisition: Share a phase prediction demonstration; test purchase intent among families already choosing space learning resources.

competitors.name: Solar System Scope
competitors.facts: Offers an online Solar System and night-sky model, mobile apps and an offline desktop version.
competitors.price: Online version is free; desktop download is listed at USD9.80; mobile purchases vary.

difference: Test guided conceptual missions rather than open-ended exploration. Existing models already cover the same subject.
risk: A cheap desktop app and free online models may satisfy buyers; educational mission authoring adds work beyond rendering.
experiment: Observe an unaided phase prediction, a later eclipse transfer question and actual purchase of the complete mission pack.
stop_rule: Consolidate into E001 if families treat it only as another curiosity topic; stop if impressive graphics fail to produce correct predictions.
overlap: Play E063 supports navigation in the actual night sky. E020 teaches modeled orbital relationships and does not identify visible stars.
rationale: Clear visual value but finite use, free substitutes and content overlap restrain priority.

name: Spatial Anatomy Learning
user: A beginning anatomy student pays to understand spatial relationships in one body system.
first_result: Trace a structure's route through a reviewed 3D model and correctly orient it from another view.
loop: Choose a bounded anatomical route
Rotate, isolate and trace structures
Compare route and landmarks with reviewed guidance
Recall the route from a new viewpoint later
return_trigger: Repeated study during an anatomy course; use may stop after the relevant assessment.
paid_value: A compact spatial-learning sequence with active route recall rather than passive viewing.

pricing.basis: Hypothesis: USD25 for a reviewed system module; zero subscription MRR.
pricing.paid: One fully reviewed body-system course with recall exercises.

compute: Local 3D display with a fixed asset budget; no generated medical models or per-user clinical data.
content_burden: Very high: anatomical accuracy, asset licensing, structure selection and explanatory navigation.
acquisition: Demonstrate one orientation problem to beginning anatomy learners; access to this audience is unverified.

competitors.name: Visible Body
competitors.facts: VB Suite combines interactive 3D anatomy models, animations, diagnostic images and physiological learning content.
competitors.price: Current paid price not verified.

difference: Test a narrow active-recall sequence for spatial routes. Rich interactive anatomy libraries are already established.
risk: Asset and expert-review costs are substantial, while broad polished products may be a better purchase than one narrow module.
experiment: Use a reviewed sample to test unaided orientation, later recall from a new angle and an actual module purchase.
stop_rule: Defer if accurate asset licensing is impractical or if users mainly need a full reference atlas rather than the proposed recall path.
overlap: Educational anatomy only; no diagnosis, rehabilitation or clinical guidance, and no Pose Coach feature duplication.
rationale: Demonstrable value but expensive specialist dependencies and finite course use make this a poor first solo lane.

name: Personal Study Recall Studio
user: A student pays to turn their own learning material into a sustainable retrieval-practice routine.
first_result: Mark several claims in pasted notes, create source-linked recall prompts and complete a first review.
loop: Paste a small set of owned study notes
Select claims and create concise recall prompts
Reveal the source and self-grade recall
Return when prompts become due and revise weak cards
return_trigger: New coursework and continuing retrieval review; assumes an active learner with recurring study needs.
paid_value: A simple durable source-to-recall workflow with transparent scheduling and editable prompts.

pricing.basis: Hypothesis: USD4/month; no observed willingness to pay.
pricing.free: A complete note-to-review loop with a limited card set.
pricing.paid: Larger study library, cross-device history and exam review planning.

compute: Local cloze generation and scheduling; pilot input capped at 10,000 characters per note. No AI-generated summaries or unlimited document processing.
content_burden: Low library burden because users supply material, but good card-authoring guidance and onboarding are necessary.
first_scope: Editable prompts and exam-date review view
acquisition: Demonstrate a messy paragraph becoming a useful recall session; assess starts from student study-method audiences.

competitors.name: RemNote
competitors.facts: Combines notes, flashcards, spaced repetition, exam scheduling and PDF-related study tools, with free and paid plans.
competitors.price: Pro displays $96 billed yearly ($8/month equivalent); Pro+AI $216 billed yearly ($18/month equivalent). Dollar currency code is not shown; monthly checkout not verified.

difference: Test a deliberately constrained source-to-recall flow that reduces card-authoring friction. This is a UX distinction within an established category.
risk: A narrower app may merely be a subset of free or paid incumbents; users must still invest effort creating accurate prompts.
experiment: Observe students create and review real prompts unaided, return on due dates without researcher reminders, then choose paid continuation over their existing tool.
stop_rule: Stop if users want automatic summaries rather than retrieval or if the simplified workflow does not displace their current study tool.
overlap: E003 is specialist passage revision; E022 handles arbitrary authored study material. No school integrations or generic chat wrapper.
rationale: Recurring learning and bounded compute are attractive, but extremely weak differentiation and input effort constrain paid value.

name: Parent-Child Reading Companion
user: A parent pays to have better comprehension conversations with a child who can follow a short story.
first_result: Read a short story together and help the child explain a character's choice using text evidence.
loop: Choose an age-appropriate reviewed story
Read and pause at a meaningful question
Use a short parent prompt to deepen the child's explanation
Return for the next story and a connected comprehension skill
return_trigger: An existing shared-reading ritual; the app must improve that ritual enough to earn repeated use.
paid_value: A growing set of enjoyable stories with subtle, useful conversation guidance for the parent.

pricing.basis: Hypothesis: USD5/month; no observed willingness to pay.
pricing.free: One complete story and parent conversation guide.
pricing.paid: Reviewed story library, new releases and a gentle skill progression.

dependencies: Original or licensed/public-domain stories with adaptation rights
compute: Curated text and optional cached narration; no generated child chat or voice analysis. Bound pilot to a small completed story collection.
content_burden: High: engaging stories, age suitability, discussion prompts and narration quality are continuing editorial work.
acquisition: Publish one printable-and-browser story conversation sample through parent reading audiences; acquisition remains unverified.

competitors.name: Epic
competitors.facts: Provides a children's digital library with books, audiobooks and videos, family trials and educator access.
competitors.price: Family trial and free educator access advertised; current family subscription price not verified.

difference: Test a compact parent conversation experience around a small curated collection. This does not compete on catalogue size.
risk: Parents already have books and free discussion advice; requiring adult participation limits convenience, while ongoing stories demand editorial effort.
experiment: Observe a family use one guide unaided, voluntarily choose another on a later reading occasion, and buy the reviewed collection.
stop_rule: Stop if prompts interrupt reading enjoyment or parents can easily reproduce the value with their existing books and free guidance.
overlap: E004 teaches decoding; E023 teaches shared comprehension. Do not duplicate E001's science-question discovery or generate personalized stories.
rationale: A real existing ritual supports recurrence, but parent effort and content economics weaken independent adoption.

name: SQL Investigation Sandbox
user: An individual beginner pays to learn reliable SQL by answering questions about a provided dataset.
first_result: Run a query that answers a small investigation and discover an error caused by duplicate or missing data.
loop: Read a concrete question about a synthetic dataset
Write and run a query locally
Inspect result differences and a minimal counterexample
Return for a new investigation reusing weak concepts
return_trigger: Course progression and occasional skill refresh; not an assumed permanent subscription.
paid_value: A coherent practical SQL course emphasizing reliable answers and debugging, with transparent grading.

pricing.basis: Hypothesis: USD25 for a complete investigation course; zero subscription MRR.
pricing.free: One complete investigation with a join or missing-data correction.
pricing.paid: Full beginner course, error history and transfer investigations.

dependencies: SQL educator review of equivalent queries and edge cases
compute: Local SQLite/WebAssembly over fixed synthetic databases with row, query-time and memory caps; no external database credentials or model calls.
content_burden: Moderate: datasets, equivalent valid answers, counterexamples and progressively useful tasks.
first_scope: In-browser SQL runner with a small dataset
A connected course from filtering to joins and aggregation
acquisition: Offer an ungated query mystery with a useful debugging reveal to SQL-learning audiences; channel access is unverified.

competitors.name: SQLBolt
competitors.facts: Provides interactive browser SQL lessons and exercises covering querying, filtering, joins and aggregation.
competitors.price: Public lesson access; no paid price listed on the opened page.

competitors.name: SQL Habit
competitors.facts: Teaches SQL and data analysis through a fictional startup and practical business/product questions.
competitors.price: Current paid price not verified.

difference: Test explicit debugging of duplicates, NULLs and misleading result sets through minimal counterexamples. Story-based SQL learning already exists.
risk: Free interactive courses and SQL Habit's established scenario approach overlap heavily; learners may finish once and leave.
experiment: Observe an unaided query and diagnosis, a later unseen dataset task, and actual purchase of the completed course after showing free alternatives.
stop_rule: Stop if learners mainly copy solutions, require personalized tutoring or choose free lessons after trying diagnostic feedback.
overlap: E002 practices spreadsheet formulas; E006 teaches general programming. This is self-contained education, not a connected analytics platform.
rationale: Very feasible and self-contained with visible value, but honest finite-course pricing and crowded alternatives keep it reserve.

name: Academic Argument Lab
user: A student pays to practice constructing evidence-backed arguments without outsourcing the writing.
first_result: Create a claim, support it from a supplied source packet and address one serious counterargument.
loop: Read a bounded question and source packet
Construct a claim–evidence–reasoning map
Check omissions against a rubric and revise a paragraph
Apply the method to another packet later
return_trigger: A finite argument-writing course and recurring assignments; direct homework import is outside the first scope.
paid_value: Reviewed practice packets, worked examples and a progression from evidence selection to counterargument.

pricing.basis: Hypothesis: USD20 for a complete introductory argument course; zero subscription MRR.
pricing.free: One complete source packet and revision exercise.
pricing.paid: A sequence of reviewed packets with saved drafts and self-assessment.

dependencies: Rubrics tested with real learner drafts
compute: Local claim mapping and rubric checklists; no generated essays or unsupported automatic writing scores. Fixed source packets bound scope.
content_burden: High: balanced prompts, source excerpts, examples and rubrics must teach actual reasoning.
first_scope: Draft revision with a transparent self-assessment rubric
acquisition: Demonstrate improvement from an unsupported claim to an evidence-backed paragraph using one free packet.

competitors.name: Kialo Edu
competitors.facts: Free discussion mapping organizes claims and pro/con reasoning for critical thinking and written communication in education.
competitors.price: Free use is explicitly advertised.

difference: Test a complete independent source-packet-to-paragraph course. Structured argument maps are already available free.
risk: Without expert feedback, self-assessment may not improve weak writing; adding per-user grading would undermine a low-cost independent product.
experiment: Observe completion of the free packet, a later independently revised argument and actual course purchase; have an educator evaluate transfer separately.
stop_rule: Stop if learners need individual teacher feedback to progress or polished-looking maps do not improve evidence use in a new paragraph.
overlap: E017 evaluates source credibility; E025 constructs a written argument. Not interview coaching, essay generation or a classroom management tool.
rationale: Meaningful distinct outcome, but the feedback gap and free alternatives make commercial validation difficult.
